inherited_methods.loss_step: freeze one assignment of private edge primes and use it only as a counterexample to bounded-length rounding
inherited_methods.lost_information: the same prime pools support a highly overlapping family of all row injections whose joint hitting number can be much larger than one
inherited_methods.consequence: the predecessor circuit is repairable by one deletion and gives no global transversal lower bound

inherited_methods.loss_step: allocate a fresh prime set to every witness so that supports are visibly disjoint
inherited_methods.lost_information: reusing row pools creates m^(d-1) distinct column products from only (d-1)m primes and can amplify repair cost combinatorially
inherited_methods.consequence: fresh-label counting is bottlenecked by prime supply and gives a substantially smaller repair bound

inherited_methods.loss_step: after finding one retained relation, stop before measuring all relations inside the same zero class
inherited_methods.lost_information: a whole grid atlas can lie in that zero class and every second-stage repair must hit the atlas rather than one edge
inherited_methods.consequence: one arbitrary post-classification deletion defeats the earlier local witness

inherited_methods.loss_step: hold d fixed while N grows
inherited_methods.lost_information: the competing losses log N/d and d log log N can be balanced by allowing d to grow slowly with N
inherited_methods.consequence: one obtains only N^(1-1/d) up to logarithms instead of a logarithmically near-linear lower bound

inherited_methods.loss_step: encode many intersecting relations through pointwise binary partitions and private prime blocks
inherited_methods.lost_information: for an unrestricted global lower bound, matching number one and a fixed top band are unnecessary; a complete grid atlas can trade those features for many more possible column products
inherited_methods.consequence: the proved cluster transversal grows only stretched-exponentially in sqrt(log N), far below the candidate grid-atlas bound

inherited_methods.method: generic random-grid union bound stated only asymptotically
inherited_methods.loss_step: replace the exact row and column marginals by independence heuristics
inherited_methods.lost_information: independence between grid vertices is unnecessary because a first-moment union bound uses only exact one-vertex marginals
inherited_methods.consequence: an unjustified independence claim would weaken or invalidate the finite transversal theorem

required_new_information: A complete-family definition using disjoint prime pools that makes every row and column product distinct and identifies the exact row and column vertex universes.
A support-minimality proof for each K_(d-1,d) relation using unique prime valuations and connectivity.
The exact finite random-grid inequality d|D_col|/m^(d-1)+|D_row|/binom(m,d)>=1 for every transversal, without assuming independence between columns.
A parameter check ensuring binom(m,d)>=m^(d-1)/d in the optimized regime, so the column term controls the stated lower bound.
A prime-number-theorem supply estimate uniform along x=N^(1/d(N)) with d(N)=floor(sqrt(log N/log log N)).
A complete logarithmic optimization proving the constant 2 in the subleading exponent and an explicit high-tail lower threshold.
A global alteration corollary that charges an arbitrary repair set after a retain-labelled zero transcript, plus a matching grid-specific upper comparator.
A scope comparison showing why the lower bound remains compatible with an o(N) transversal and does not settle Erdos 786.
